overview: This file documents U.S.–Japanese negotiations and preparations for Richard Halliburton and aviator Moye W. Stephens Jr. to fly over Japanese-ruled Taiwan in 1931–1932. Japan offered permission subject to a prescribed route and regulations, while making it conditional upon reciprocal American authorization for a Japanese newspaper-sponsored aircraft bound for Australia to land at Manila. Later correspondence from the American consul at Xiamen transmitted a Japanese-provided map of a temporary Taiwan landing field but reported that the proposed Halliburton–Stephens flight had apparently been abandoned; the map was also passed to the U.S. Asiatic Fleet.

people.name: Richard Halliburton
people.role: American traveler and flier involved in the proposed flight over Taiwan

people.name: Moye W. Stephens Jr.
people.role: American aviator involved in the proposed flight over Taiwan; his surname is rendered “Stevens” in the file

subfiles.title: Cross-reference for Forbes telegram on the proposed Taiwan flight
subfiles.about: The sheet directs researchers to another file for Forbes’s telegram concerning Japanese conditions for the Halliburton–Stephens flight over Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Japan had no objection to the proposed Taiwan flight if route rules were followed, conditioned on a Manila landing.

subfiles.title: Forbes telegram on conditional Japanese approval of the Taiwan flight
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forbes reports that Japan would permit the Halliburton–Stephens flight if the United States granted landing rights at Manila to a Japanese aircraft.
subfiles.summary: Japan's Foreign Office allowed the Taiwan overflight if regulations were followed, tied to approving a Nagoya-sponsored Japan-Australia flight's Manila landing; Forbes asked where to send the rules.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference for Franklin’s report and landing-field map
subfiles.about: The sheet points to Franklin’s report concerning a map supplied for the proposed Halliburton–Stephens flight over Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: a Japanese-consul-supplied map showed a Taiwan military drill ground prepared as a temporary landing field, likely 1932 not 1938.

subfiles.title: Franklin report No. 47 on the proposed flight to Taiwan
subfiles.from: Lynn W. Franklin, American Consul at Xiamen
subfiles.to: Nelson Trusler Johnson, American Minister at Beijing
subfiles.about: Franklin forwards a Japanese map of a temporary Taiwan landing field and reports that the proposed flight apparently will not occur.
subfiles.summary: Franklin encloses a Japanese-consul map of a Taiwan drill ground prepared as a landing field, reporting the flight was called off, and shared it with the Asiatic Fleet via USS Stewart.

subfiles.title: Map of landing field in Formosa
subfiles.about: The enclosure depicts the Taiwan landing field described in Franklin’s report.
subfiles.summary: Map labeled 'Landing Field - Formosa,' about 150 meters above sea level, shows the drill ground prepared temporarily for Halliburton and Stephens.

interest: Shows a private aviation stunt entangled with Japan-U.S. reciprocal landing rights and naval intelligence over Taiwan.
